title: Printing Press Operators
description: Set up and operate digital, letterpress, lithographic, flexographic, gravure, or other printing machines. Includes short-run offset printing presses.

tasks.text: Adjust ink fountain flow rates.
Feed paper through press cylinders and adjust feed and tension controls.
Secure printing plates to printing units and adjust tolerances.
Change press plates, blankets, or cylinders, as required.
Load presses with paper and make necessary adjustments, according to paper size.
Clean ink fountains, plates, or printing unit cylinders when press runs are completed.
Obtain or mix inks and fill ink fountains.
Clean or oil presses or make minor repairs, using hand tools.
Download or scan files to be printed, using printing production software.
Adjust digital files to alter print elements, such as fonts, graphics, or color separations.
Input production job settings into workstation terminals that control automated printing systems.
Download completed jobs to archive media so that questions can be answered or jobs replicated.
Start presses and pull proofs to check for ink coverage and density, alignment, and registration.
Collect and inspect random samples during print runs to identify any necessary adjustments.
Examine job orders to determine quantities to be printed, stock specifications, colors, or special printing instructions.
Monitor environmental factors, such as humidity and temperature, that may impact equipment performance and make necessary adjustments.
Direct or monitor work of press crews.
Control workflow scheduling or job tracking, using computer database software.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Verify that paper and ink meet the specifications for a given job.
Monitor automated press operation systems and respond to fault, error, or alert messages.
Maintain time or production records.
Monitor inventory levels on a regular basis, ordering or requesting additional supplies, as necessary.
Set up or operate auxiliary equipment, such as cutting, folding, plate-making, drilling, or laminating machines.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Equipment Maintenance
skills.def: Performing routine maintenance on equipment and determining when and what kind of maintenance is needed.

skills.name: Troubleshooting
skills.def: Determining causes of operating errors and deciding what to do about it.

skills.name: Repairing
skills.def: Repairing machines or systems using the needed tools.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, Corel CorelDraw Graphics Suite, Graphics software.

skills.name: Desktop publishing software
skills.def: Software to create or edit text and graphics into documents such as books, magazines, brochures, or manuals. Examples: Adobe InDesign, Adobe PageMaker, Enfocus PitStop Pro, QuarkXPress.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Adobe Acrobat, Adobe LifeCycle Production Print ES3, Xerox FreeFlow Print Server.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Electronics for Imaging EFI Monarch, Electronics for Imaging EFI Pace, SAP software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.
